name: Bullish Seagull Spread
summary: Buy a call spread financed by selling an OTM put; a three-strike, near-zero-cost bullish structure with downside share-purchase obligation.

legs.strike_rule: put delta -0.15 to -0.25, at or below a defined support level (cash-secured)
ATM or slightly OTM, call delta 0.45-0.55
call delta 0.20-0.25, at or above the price target

net: either (target zero cost or a small credit)
when_to_use: A name you have a genuine bullish thesis on and would be willing to own at the short put strike, with a clear technical support below and a resistance target above. Works best when skew is steep (the OTM put is expensive), which is the normal state for equities.
max_profit: (short call strike - long call strike) x 100 + net credit (or - net debit)
max_loss: (short put strike x 100) - net credit, on a move to zero. Large but bounded.
breakevens: upside breakeven = long call strike + debit/100 (or none if opened for a credit); downside breakeven = short put strike - credit/100

greeks.gamma: mixed - positive around the long call, negative around the short put

entry_rules: Target a net cost between -0.10 and +0.10 per share (i.e. near zero); reject any fill costing more than 15% of the call spread width.
Short put strike must sit at or below a support level identified from at least 60 sessions of price history, and at delta between -0.15 and -0.25.
The short put MUST be fully cash-secured (reserve strike x 100 - credit). Uncollateralized is level 4.
Underlying price <= $120 so the cash-secured put is under 25% of a $50k account.
All three strikes: OI >= 500, per-leg spread <= max($0.05, 10% of mid).
Single 3-leg order at mid, accept mid + $0.03.
management_rules: Profit target: close at 65% of the call spread's max value.
Close at 21 DTE regardless of P/L.
Tested-down rule: if spot closes below the short put strike, close the whole structure; do not roll into a bigger obligation.
Stop: close if the short put delta reaches -0.45.
Never let the call spread expire worthless while the short put remains open - close as one package.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the short put and the short call are both assignable. Flatten every leg by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short put immediately if ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the call spread before the ex-date if the short call is ITM with extrinsic below the declared dividend.
Close any ITM short leg by 2 DTE unconditionally.
assignment_risk: Short put assignment buys 100 shares at the put strike with no offsetting long put - the defining risk of a seagull. The short call is covered by the long call, so its assignment leaves a temporary short stock position hedged by the long call. The put leg is what makes this a Level-3-with-cash-secured structure rather than a simple spread.
buying_power: Cash-secured put (strike x 100 - credit) plus the call spread's debit. The put leg dominates.
common_mistakes: Selling a put on a name you do not actually want to own; treating 'zero cost' as 'zero risk'; putting the short put at a strike chosen for premium rather than for support; carrying the short put into expiry.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended - the naked-equivalent short put creates same-day share delivery risk and the call spread needs time to work.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
